title: Original Visual Grammar
summary: Two project-native diagrams make the route from representation to consequence inspectable, including the gates and repair paths that prevent class language or word power from becoming mystical, automatic, or reductionist.

sourceImagePolicy.note: The unidentified software-design reference pages remain internal-only. These diagrams use only the suite's abstract requirements and the website's own visual system; no source pixels, illustrations, or page layouts are reproduced.

diagrams.title: From specification to consequence
diagrams.proposition: A class matters through what its instances can represent, do, preserve, and repair.
diagrams.description: The sequence begins with a declared class, follows a concrete instance through state and admissible operation, then tests the resulting consequence against the class's invariants.
diagrams.accessibleSummary: Class specifies distinctions and invariants. An instance embodies that specification in a current state. An admissible operation changes the state and produces a consequence. An invariant check either permits closure or routes the defect through witness, responsibility, repair, and revision before returning to state.

path.label: Class
path.description: Declares entities, distinctions, invariants, methods, and interfaces.

path.label: Instance
path.description: Embodies the specification as a concrete institution, system, or object.

path.label: State
path.description: Locates the instance in its present conditions, relations, and obligations.

path.label: Operation
path.description: Acts through a permitted method or interface under declared constraints.

path.label: Consequence
path.description: Produces a new state whose effects can be observed, attributed, and tested.

feedback.question: Did the operation preserve what the class said must remain true?
feedback.returnDescription: Repair changes the represented state or revises the class before the next operation is admitted.

diagrams.title: From symbol to material consequence
diagrams.proposition: A word becomes consequential only through an interpreter, recognized authority, and an executable path.
diagrams.description: The symbol does not act by itself. A procedure interprets it, a system recognizes a distinction, and an authority gate determines whether any operation may follow.
diagrams.accessibleSummary: A symbol enters an interpreter or procedure. The system recognizes a distinction and classification. An authority and standing gate decides whether an operation is admissible. Execution changes state and produces consequence. A contestability check either explains or affirms the result, or routes it through appeal, witness, responsibility, and repair before correction returns to the state transition.

path.label: Symbol
path.description: A word, mark, credential, record, declaration, or label is presented.

path.label: Interpreter
path.description: A grammar, compiler, rule, clerk, court, or procedure assigns meaning.

path.label: Classification
path.description: The system recognizes an entity, distinction, status, or obligation.

path.label: Authority
path.description: Standing, evidence, jurisdiction, and permission determine whether action is valid.

path.label: Operation
path.description: An action becomes admissible, prohibited, required, or available.

path.label: State transition
path.description: The operative system changes a represented or material condition.

path.label: Consequence
path.description: Access, obligation, resource, standing, risk, or force is redistributed.

feedback.question: Can the classification, authority, and resulting action be explained and challenged?
feedback.returnDescription: A valid correction changes the record, rule, authority decision, or transition rather than pretending the earlier consequence never occurred.

safeguards: A person is not exhausted by any software or institutional representation.
A useful analogy is not an established formal equivalence.
A symbol has no automatic or mystical force; consequence requires interpretation, authority, and execution.
Repair may change future state and responsibility without erasing elapsed consequence.
claimCeiling: These diagrams are explanatory models for the current public argument. They do not establish a formal class of worlds, prove cross-domain equivalence, reduce persons or institutions to software objects, or imply that words act without interpreters, authority, records, enforcement, and repair.
